% THE DEFECT, kept compiling on purpose: the conversion done the way the skill
% used to recommend -- a hand-rolled title frame instead of \maketitle, and the
% beamer folded subtitle left in \title. It renders, it is the right shape, and
% nothing in the log says anything is wrong.
%
% What it costs, and what assert-after.sh measures:
%   * /S /H1 = 0. Plain text in a frame is not tagged as anything, so the deck's
%     title is not a heading at all. A-HEADINGS had to hand-write the H1 back for
%     exactly this reason; the native path does not.
%   * The long argument of \title is never rendered, so it silently duplicates
%     the frame's text and drifts from it. Here they already disagree -- the frame
%     says "Constraint Satisfaction", \title says something else, and the only
%     place that shows is the PDF metadata, which nobody looks at.
%
% The folded subtitle is left in \title deliberately: it is what the beamer source
% says, and it is the second thing a conversion has to fix. It does no harm HERE,
% because without \maketitle the title element never runs -- which is precisely
% why the defect is invisible until you move to the native title page.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard={a-4,ua-2}, tagging=on}

\hypersetup{pdfauthor={A. Lecturer}}
